idiom_name: early-return/throw guards; ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull for argument checks
implementation_notes: C# guards are if plus return or throw, with pattern forms (is null, is not { }, switch case guards) keeping the condition compact. Since .NET 6 the BCL supplies ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(argument), whose CallerArgumentExpression-based paramName replaces the hand-written if (x is null) throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(x)) block while keeping the happy path flat; the same call also feeds nullable reference analysis, which narrows the rest of the method. Debug.Assert/Trace.Assert from System.Diagnostics are for invariants, not for validating input.
pitfalls: Nullable flow analysis forgets the narrowing across fields, properties, callbacks and async boundaries; a stored Order? field still needs a re-check or an explicit accessor.
Debug.Assert is compiled out of release builds: like assert elsewhere it documents invariants and never validates arguments.

Every exception a guard throws is part of the method contract; a caller that must catch it cannot discover it from the signature, so document the guard and prefer the Argument* exception family for argument errors.
